analysis: Both supplied units are CHANGELOG.md head-text excerpts (lines 223-600). Only documentation changed, so there is no executable security regression in them. The entries describe security-relevant code changes whose source was not supplied, so a later pass must verify them. Those claims are untrusted evidence. (1) Frozen legacy MDM cohort and /v1/enroll now needing a linked provider token plus a signed SE-key proof (lines 298-307). Relevant: TB-005, TB-009, TB-011, T-036, T-052, T-057. (2) Base rewards gated on macOS 27+ and qualified App Attest authorization (line 301). Relevant: T-055, T-060. (3) Coordinator cache-routing persistence across restarts (lines 472-476). It stores holders and demand with no prompts or raw chain hashes, which may extend the same-account TTFT oracle in T-041/SEC-035. The new store is not covered by the TTL/KEK-wipe mitigations in the threat model. (4) SSD write budget raised from 150 to 750 GB/day (line 513), plus the 30-minute TTL already acknowledged in T-041 (lines 594-595). (5) Removal of top-level user/metadata/safety_identifier/prompt_cache_key from provider-bound bodies (line 278), consistent with the header note. (6) Removal of the unauthenticated provider earnings lookup (line 570, T-031) and fail-closed attestation challenges (line 572). (7) Billing and settlement changes to referral rewards and cache-read pricing (lines 228-232, 547-553), relevant to A-009/TB-008. No concrete defect is evidenced from the changelog alone. Verify the backing code against T-036, T-041, T-053 and T-060, and check that the threat model covers the persisted cache-routing state.
